title: Maths Week Scotland - Dundee University
text: Welcome! This site was created in 2026 at the University of Dundee for our Maths Trial at the Dundee Botanic Gardens, as part of the wider Maths Week Scotland programme of events. It is designed to be used while exploring the Botanic Gardens and using a smart-phone to scan QR barcodes taking you to individual pages here.

title: Phyllotaxis
text:
Plants space their leaves using specific divergence angles (the angular degree separation between successive leaves on a stem), which is known as phyllotaxis. Phyllotaxis has common characteristic across plant species, which are mathematically characterised in a small number of phyllotactic patterns.
Which of the following leaf arrangement pattern do you find in this plant?

title: Phyllotaxis
text:
Distichous (\(180^\circ\))
Leaves alternate on opposite sides of the stem in a single flat plane.

title: Phyllotaxis
text:
Fibonacci Spiral (\(137.5^\circ\))
Leaves wind in a tight spiral using the golden angle, maximising space and light efficiency.

title: Phyllotaxis
text:
Decussate (\(90^\circ\))
Successive pairs of leaves sit at right angles to each other.

title: Phyllotaxis
text:
Tricussate (\(60^\circ\))
Whorls feature three leaves per node, rotated evenly around the stem.

title: Phyllotaxis Statistics
text: Plant species optimize their solar capture and space packing using specific evolutionary patterns. While the golden angle (\(137.5^\circ\)) is famous, species also commonly exhibit alternate patterns like distichous (\(180^\circ\)), decussate (\(90^\circ\)), or tristichous (\(120^\circ\)) arrangements. In this hands-on investigation, your team will act as field data scientists to harvest real-world biological samples, aggregate multi-species raw tallies, and build a categorical frequency distribution to determine which divergence architecture dominates the local ecosystem.
